cards.explanation: The answer is Bethsaida, friends. Luke says Jesus took the apostles away privately and withdrew to a town called Bethsaida (Luke 9:10). The apostles are the Twelve, the men Jesus sent out earlier (Luke 6:13; 9:1, 2). Just a quiet getaway with His closest followers, and you know how well quiet worked out.

The answer is False. Luke 9:11 says that He welcomed them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God. No sending anybody away, no sign on the door. A crowd follows Him and He makes room for them anyway.

The answer is heals, friends. The text says He healed those who needed healing (Luke 9:11). So the crowd got teaching about the kingdom of God and healing from Him. That's a lot of work, and the Twelve haven't even brought up food yet.

The answer is to send them off to find food and lodging, friends. The Twelve said, "Dismiss the crowd so they can go to the surrounding villages and countryside for lodging and provisions." (Luke 9:12) They also pointed out that they were in a desolate place. So their plan was to send everyone off to find a place to stay and something to eat.

The answer is five loaves and two fish, bakers. The disciples answered, "We have only five loaves of bread and two fish…" (Luke 9:13). That was their answer to "You give them something to eat." I've seen a bigger stash in my cookie jar on a slow Tuesday.

The answer is to sit down in groups of about fifty, friends. Jesus told His disciples, "Have them sit down in groups of about fifty each." (Luke 9:14) That was for about five thousand men. I'll leave the math to you, but that's a lot of little groups.

The answer is True. Luke 9:15 says, "They did so, and everyone was seated." The disciples did what Jesus asked, and the whole crowd sat down. Getting thousands of people settled in groups is no small thing, friends.

The answer is HEAVEN, friends! Luke 9:16 says Jesus took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, spoke a blessing and broke them. Five loaves and two fish in front of about five thousand men (Luke 9:14), and the first thing He does is look up. Me? I'd be counting the dough three times and sweating through my apron.

The answer is False. After He broke the loaves and fish, Jesus "…gave them to the disciples to set before the people." (Luke 9:16) The disciples carried the food out to the crowd. They had been told to feed the people, and now they had food in their hands.
The answer is satisfied, friends. Luke 9:17 says, "They all ate and were satisfied…" Five loaves and two fish, about five thousand men, and all of them satisfied. Everyone had enough.

The answer is twelve basketfuls, bakers! Luke 9:17 says the disciples "…picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over." After feeding about five thousand men, there was still food left to gather. I've never had that problem with a cookie tray.
